content.audience: Synthetic study task for the thesis AI-only run: a teacher computing final grades
content.problem_statement: Compute each student's weighted final grade from a CSV of quiz, exam and project scores, with the lowest quiz dropped, exact half-up rounding, letter grades, an optional curve and the class average. This is a frozen synthetic task for the thesis AI-only run, not a customer product.

user_flows.name: Final grades
steps: Pipe the score CSV into the CLI
Read each student's final grade and letter, best first, and the class average

user_flows.name: Curve
steps: Read the grades with N points added

user_flows.name: Bad CSV
steps: Pipe a CSV with a wrong header or row
Read the error naming the line and exit status 1

user_flows.name: Bad arguments
steps: Run with an argument the CLI does not accept
Read invalid arguments and exit status 2

scope: Python 3.8+ standard library only, entry point src/main.py, all code under src
Read all of stdin and split it into lines on \n, numbered from 1. If the text ends with \n, the empty piece after it is not a line
Line 1 must be the header student,kind,score (leading and trailing whitespace ignored); otherwise, or when there is no line at all, print exactly: error: line 1 and exit 1
Each later line, trimmed, is skipped when empty

Otherwise it has exactly three comma-separated cells, each trimmed: student (a lowercase letter followed by up to 19 lowercase letters, digits or underscores), kind (quiz, exam or project) and score (an integer 0 to 100 written without leading zeros or sign)
A bad row prints exactly: error: line N (N its line number), prints nothing else, and exits 1. Only the first bad line is reported
For each student and kind, the kind's score is the mean of that student's scores of that kind. If a student has 3 or more quiz scores, drop exactly one lowest quiz score before taking the quiz mean
The final grade is 0.3 x quiz + 0.5 x exam + 0.2 x project, computed exactly. A kind with no scores counts as 0 and the student is incomplete
Round the final grade half up to one decimal place, exactly (for example 84.25 becomes 84.3 and 84.249 becomes 84.2). Do not use binary floating point for this
--curve N (an integer 0 to 10) adds N to every rounded final grade, at most 100.0. Without it N is 0
The letter comes from the curved grade: A at 90.0 or above, B at 80.0, C at 70.0, D at 60.0, otherwise F

Print one line per student: student, space, curved grade with exactly one decimal, space, letter, and the word incomplete after one more space if incomplete. Order by curved grade descending, then student name ascending (plain string order)

Then print class average X, where X is the mean of the printed curved grades rounded half up to one decimal. With a header but no data rows print exactly: no students. Each output line ends with \n. Exit 0
Arguments are either none or exactly --curve N. Anything else prints exactly: invalid arguments, then \n, and exits 2
No files, network, environment variables or third-party packages

risks.risk: Six tasks written by one author do not establish general build quality
risks.mitigation: Report results only for these frozen tasks, this route, model and role prompts, as the AI-only arm alone

risks.risk: Held-out cases leak to the builder
risks.mitigation: The studio hides held-out studio cases from builder and reviewer; extended cases are never entered into the studio; the repository copy is never sent to runtime roles

obligations: Keep this frozen version unchanged; a change needs a new version and is reported as a deviation
